title: Cold Email Isn't Dead: The 5 Fixes Guide
description: The 5 fixes behind our 82,671-email campaign with 2,146 interested leads: tracking off, smaller lists, clean lists, short emails and real follow-ups.
lead: This is the full 5 fixes guide from the reel. The reel showed 2 fixes. Here are all 5, the same ones behind our 82,671 emails, 2,429 replies and 2,146 interested leads.
insider: These numbers are from our own agency client campaign (June 1 to October 19, 2026), with open tracking off the whole time. Only **6 of 76,081** people asked to be removed. You can copy the 5 fixes yourself. If you'd rather have them running next month without learning it all, that's exactly what we do.

blocks.text: Open tracking adds a hidden pixel to every email, and inbox providers notice. Hunter.io's 2026 data (31 million emails) showed **7.4% replies with tracking off vs 4.4% with it on**. Judge your campaign by replies, not opens.
In the same Hunter.io data, lists of **21 to 50 people got 6.2% replies vs 2.4% for lists of 500+**. Small lists force you to target better and write for one type of buyer.

items: Split your big list by industry, job title and company size.
Write one version of the email for each small group.
Mention what that group has in common in the first line.

blocks.text: Fix 3: Verify every email before you send

Bounces tell inbox providers you bought a bad list. Keep bounces **under 2%**. Run every list through an email verifier and remove risky and catch-all addresses you can't confirm. Our campaigns run between 0.45% and 3.08% bounce, and we pause any inbox that goes over.
Fix 4: Keep it short and plain

items: Under 80 words, so it fits on one phone screen
Plain text: no images, no fancy design
One link at most, or none in the first email
One small question at the end, like "Worth a look?"

blocks.text: Most replies come after the first email. Send 3 to 4 emails a few days apart, and give each follow-up a new angle, not "just bumping this up". Comment THREE on our reels for the email 3 template.

blocks.label: Bottom line
blocks.text: Cold email isn't dead. Bad cold email is.

faq.q: If tracking is off, how do I know it's working?
faq.a: Count replies and booked calls. Those are the numbers that pay you anyway.
In the U.S. it is, if you follow CAN-SPAM rules. Our [legal guide](/blog/is-cold-email-legal.html) explains it in plain English.
